raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

In Rust frontend mode (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) a scheduler that is busy with a long prefill fails `/health_generate` even though it is alive, so a router in front of it marks a healthy engine unhealthy.

A busy scheduler skips health probes and acknowledges them after its next step. That acknowledgement is sent to the zmq tokenizer socket, which nothing reads in Rust mode:

- the Rust probe counts only decode-batch frames as scheduler activity, so it sees nothing until the prefill finishes and the probe times out;
- every skipped probe also queues one message on the unread socket, which is unbounded (`SNDHWM 0`).

## Modifications

- In Rust mode the scheduler pushes the acknowledgement onto the Rust response ring as a new bodiless frame, `DISPATCH_TAG_HEALTH_ACK` (`Server.push_health_ack` / `RustServer.push_health_ack`).
- The Rust dispatcher counts that frame as scheduler activity, the same way the Python `TokenizerManager` counts `HealthCheckOutput`.
- Rust probes share one heartbeat, so one acknowledgement per step answers every probe skipped so far; the scheduler clears its pending-probe queue instead of answering them one per step. A skipped probe now passes within one scheduler step. A single step longer than the client timeout still fails, by design.
- The Python frontend path is unchanged.
- Tests: `skipped_probe_passes_on_health_ack_and_cleans_up` replaces `healthy_probe_uses_shared_activity_and_cleans_up` in `handle.rs` and drives the probe through a real `Dispatcher` with an acknowledgement frame instead of bumping the counter by hand; `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_health_check_signal.py` pins the scheduler side for both modes (the Rust-mode case fails on `main`).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model-output path changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the new frame is one byte per scheduler step, and only while a probe is pending.

Run locally on this branch:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` (364 passed).
- `pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_health_check_signal.py` (2 passed; the Rust-mode case fails on `main` with `push_health_ack` never called).
- pre-commit hooks for the touched files (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, the registered-test checks).

Not run here: a real-server reproduction with a long chunked prefill while `/health_generate` is probed under a short client timeout.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -5112,11 +5112,18 @@ def maybe_send_health_check_signal(self):
             # Return some signal for the health check.
             # This is used to prevent the health check signal being blocked by long context prefill.
             # However, one minor issue is that this code path does not check the status of detokenizer manager.
-            self.ipc_channels.send_to_tokenizer.send_output(
-                HealthCheckOutput(
-                    http_worker_ipc=self.return_health_check_ipcs.popleft()
+            if self.rust_server is not None:
+                # The zmq tokenizer socket is not consumed in Rust mode. Rust
+                # probes share one heartbeat, so one acknowledgement answers
+                # every probe skipped so far.
+                self.return_health_check_ipcs.clear()
+                self.rust_server.push_health_ack()
+            else:
+                self.ipc_channels.send_to_tokenizer.send_output(
+                    HealthCheckOutput(
+                        http_worker_ipc=self.return_health_check_ipcs.popleft()
+                    )
                 )
-            )
 
     def add_external_corpus(
         self, recv_req: AddExternalCorpusReqInput

@@ -373,6 +373,10 @@ def push_control_output(self, recv_req, output) -> None:
 
         self.server.push_control_result(recv_req.rid, encoded)
 
+    def push_health_ack(self) -> None:
+        """Acknowledge the health probes skipped while the scheduler was busy."""
+        self.server.push_health_ack()
+
     def push_generation(self, payload: BatchTokenIDOutput) -> None:
         """Egress redirect for generation output (replaces the zmq detokenizer).

@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+"""A busy scheduler acknowledges the health probes it skipped after each step.
+
+The Python frontend reads the acknowledgement from the zmq tokenizer socket.
+The embedded Rust server does not consume that socket, so in Rust mode the
+acknowledgement goes on its response ring instead.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from collections import deque
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import HealthCheckOutput  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.rust_server.server import RustServer  # noqa: E402
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestHealthCheckSignal(CustomTestCase):
+    def _scheduler(self, rust_server, pending) -> Scheduler:
+        s = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+        s.rust_server = rust_server
+        s.ipc_channels = MagicMock()
+        s.return_health_check_ipcs = deque(pending)
+        return s
+
+    def test_rust_mode_acknowledges_all_skipped_probes_on_the_ring(self):
+        server = MagicMock()
+        s = self._scheduler(RustServer(server, http_port=0), [None, None])
+
+        s.maybe_send_health_check_signal()
+        s.maybe_send_health_check_signal()
+
+        server.push_health_ack.assert_called_once_with()
+        self.assertFalse(s.return_health_check_ipcs)
+        s.ipc_channels.send_to_tokenizer.send_output.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_python_mode_acknowledges_one_probe_per_step_on_zmq(self):
+        s = self._scheduler(None, ["ipc-a", "ipc-b"])
+
+        s.maybe_send_health_check_signal()
+
+        (output,), _ = s.ipc_channels.send_to_tokenizer.send_output.call_args
+        self.assertIsInstance(output, HealthCheckOutput)
+        self.assertEqual(output.http_worker_ipc, "ipc-a")
+        self.assertEqual(list(s.return_health_check_ipcs), ["ipc-b"])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
